merger_description:
Samsung Biologics proposes to make an all-cash public tender offer to acquire all publicly held registered shares of the PolyPeptide Group AG (the **Target**). Under the Transaction Agreement, the Target will recommend the tender offer for acceptance by the holders of the Target’s shares (the **Acquisition**).  

  

Draupnir Holding B.V. (the largest individual shareholder of the Target) also signed a Tender Undertaking with Samsung Biologics pursuant to which it agreed to tender all its shares corresponding to approximately 55.65% of the Target’s total outstanding shares (excluding treasury shares). The all-cash public tender offer is worth approximately CHF 1.46 billion (~AUD 2.59 billion).  

  

Samsung Biologics, headquartered in South Korea, is a contract development and manufacturing organisation (**CDMO**) which offers services that range from research and development to commercial manufacturing. Samsung Biologics provides CDMO services for active pharmaceutical ingredients (**APIs**) and finished drug products, as well as contract research organisation services.   

  

Samsung Biologics is listed on the Korean stock exchange and is currently owned by Samsung C&T Corporation (43.06%), Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. (31.22%) and others (25.72%).   

  

The Target is headquartered in Switzerland, is a specialised global CDMO for peptide-based APIs using chemically synthesised production methods. It services primarily pharma and biotech customers by offering products and services from pre-clinical to commercial stages. The Target also produces a range of generic peptides.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Samsung Biologics
and PolyPeptide Group AG in the supply of CDMO services
for APIs in Australia
b. the parties’ combined share in the supply of CDMO services
for APIs globally is low and the increase in share of supply
arising from the Acquisition would be small
c. there are alternative suppliers of CDMO services for APIs in
Australia and globally.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
